object_description: three-part, finely structured L-shaped timber volume stepping with the rising terrain
geometry_property: separate gymnasium volume on the slope
design_condition: the L-shaped volume sits at the lower northern edge of the perimeter and is integrated into the rising terrain with access points at every level, keeping the slope permeable for downdraughts

positive: The compact L-shaped volume forms a successful, harmonious ensemble with the existing school complex
Projections and recesses seek a spatial interweaving with the surroundings
The covered entrance area becomes the hinge between the buildings and the existing pine forest
The structured outdoor area has a high degree of permeability towards the slope, favourable for downdraughts
Existing groups of trees are to become an inviting grove
The school is cleverly integrated into the rising terrain with access points at all levels
The covered outdoor entrance hall becomes the gathering centre of the complex with good outdoor access
The airy interpenetration of inside and outside continues on the upper floors with open decks and protective balconies
These decks could be suitable places for students to stay during short breaks
All clusters have a fixed core and can be flexibly subdivided within the two-sided exposed space
The clusters can be used in different arrangements depending on the educational concept, which users would greatly appreciate
The sports facilities are accessible from the lower level and easy to find for non-school users
The swimming pool is conveniently located and well lit under the school wing
Despite five storeys in places the light timber architecture reads credibly as a pavilion-like building well suited to a primary school
The carefully elaborated project shows high qualities and coherence between expression, outdoor areas and flexibility
As a place for schoolchildren to deal with the urban climate it testifies to a specific, humane attitude
negative: The artificial ventilation concept seems incomprehensible under these otherwise optimal conditions
The external connecting staircases could be left open
The building should be more open and permeable, with little interaction between the levels and the two schools
The gymnasium as a separate volume on the slope requires considerable excavation
The resulting high factor of underbuilt area undermines the otherwise sensitive handling of the situation
Large areas spread out in the basement together with pool and underground parking
The enormous amount of terrain work is at odds with the light, simply structured timber architecture
Large facade developments, redundant accesses and oversized areas cause the project to overshoot the cost target by far
